title: Russell US Style indexes — conditional quarter-end recapping effective at the open (24% / 4.8%-above-48% breach test struck on the 2026-09-25 close), one session ahead of the S&P Select Sector reweight
source: EST: owner-published, re-fetched and re-extracted independently this session from TWO documents rather than one. (1) FTSE Russell, "Frequently Asked Questions -- Russell US Equity Indexes", July 2026 (lseg.com dam policy-documents, ftse-faq-document-russell-us-equity-2026.pdf, HTTP 200, 198,134 bytes -- reproducing the byte count both siblings recorded; 19 content streams inflated and text-extracted in-session 2026-09-08). Its dated four-column schedule table carries, verbatim, "Russell US Style Quarter-end Capping Cut-Off Date | 26 March 2026 | 25 June 2026 | 25 SEPTEMBER 2026 | 28 December 2026" and "Russell US Style Quarter-end Capping Effective Date (open of, if applicable) | 31 March 2026 | 30 June 2026 | 30 SEPTEMBER 2026 | 31 December 2026". (2) NEW THIS SESSION, and the document neither sibling read: FTSE Russell, "Capping Methodology Guide", v5.4, SEPTEMBER 2026 (lseg.com dam policy-documents, capping-methodology-guide.pdf, HTTP 200, 652,008 bytes, 62 streams inflated) -- the guide the FAQ points to, in its current version. It states the standing rule in a table rather than one year's dates: reference date "T-3", effective "Last business day in Mar, Jun, Sep and Dec", trigger "No company is greater than 24%, and all companies that have a weight greater than 4.8% in aggregate are no more than 48% of the index", scheme "RIC 22.5/45". THE INTERNAL CHECK IS EXACT AND IS THIS SESSION'S OWN: the T-3 rule reproduces ALL FOUR of the owner's published 2026 cut-off dates to the day, including the holiday-aware December one (last business day 31 Dec -> T-1 30 Dec, T-2 29 Dec, T-3 28 Dec, stepping over Christmas Day). THE EVENT IS CONDITIONAL BY CONSTRUCTION and is labelled so -- the guide says "Where a breach is identified, the index is recapped ... If no breach is identified, no changes are made." Filed estimate because this lane may not flip a status without an IR:/BLS:/FED: primary, the confirmed-tier prefixes have no member for an index owner's own published methodology, and the FAQ table carries the owner's caveat "NOTE: Dates may be subject to change. Clients will be notified of any changes." The DATE is not in doubt -- the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence. Canonical file written by this event's own initial research after reading the single proposal carrying this id in full, checked 2026-09-08
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THIS EVENT'S OWN INITIAL RESEARCH (2026-09-08), which read proposals/russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2026-09-30.from-russell-quarterly-ipo-review-effective-2026-09-21.json in full first, then re-fetched the owner's documents rather than inheriting the proposal's readings. Ledger: docs/research/events/russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2026-09-30.md. THE PROPOSAL'S SCOPE CLAIM IS REFUTED AND THAT IS THIS RESEARCH'S MAIN CORRECTION. The proposal wrote that the framework applies only to "applicable capped Russell US Style Indexes" and concluded "nothing here reaches the names this house watches unless it holds a capped style product". The premise is right and the conclusion is wrong: effective at the open of 2025-03-24 the STANDARD Russell US Style Indexes became the capped ones (the uncapped versions were renamed with "Benchmark" in the name), and the iShares Trust's own SEC Form 497 names EIGHT funds tracking them -- IWF, IWD, IWY, IWX, IWP, IWS, IWO, IWN -- carrying about $294.6B of ETF assets between them as read this session, IWF alone at $126.03B. The proposal's narrower statement that IWM and the broad Russell trackers are untouched remains TRUE (they track the cap-weighted Russell 1000/2000, which the owner excludes by name); it simply pointed at the wrong instrument. THE FLOW IS REAL BUT THE TEST ALMOST NEVER FIRES, AND THE RESEARCH QUANTIFIED WHY: the quarter-end check is a BACKSTOP sitting behind the quarterly capping review, which is scheduled 16 days earlier (style capping cut-off 2026-09-09, effective at the 2026-09-21 open) and resets the >4.5% cohort to 45%. IWY's cohort sits at 46.79% (2026-09-04, holdings 2026-08-27 drifted on daily closes), so the 09-09 review will recap it; from a 45% reset the 09-25 test needs the cohort to beat its own index by 6.67% over the 12 intervening sessions, which cleared in 50 of 1,243 rolling 12-session windows over five years = 4.02%. Without that recap the same test needs only +2.59% and clears in 28.96% of windows. The quarterly cap cuts the breach probability roughly SEVENFOLD; that is the mechanical finding. Single-name leg is dead everywhere -- NVDA, the largest weight in the family, is 16.38% in IWY against a 22.5% cap and a 24% trigger. Five of the eight funds cannot breach by construction (IWP top holding 3.09%, IWS 0.82%, IWO 0.67%, IWN 0.63% -- no constituent within reach of 4.8%, so the cohort is empty); IWD's cohort is 16.40% and IWX's 22.79%, both far under 48%. THE PROPOSAL'S CORRELATION CLAIM IS ALSO CORRECTED: it said the Russell and S&P conditional recaps land on "the SAME OPEN". They do not. Russell is effective at the OPEN of 2026-09-30, so trackers trade the 2026-09-29 close; sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2026-09-30 is effective AFTER the 2026-09-30 close, so it trades the 09-30 close. One session apart, on different reference dates (Russell T-3 = 09-25; S&P second-to-last business day = 09-29) and different universes (mega-cap growth vs GICS sectors). The pairing is a quarter-end corridor, not a single concentrated session. Impact LOW and symbols deliberately EMPTY, on evidence rather than by inheritance: the measured breach probability is 4.02%, a fired recap moves about 3pp of IWY's $15.94B (about $478M) across five mega caps that each trade multiples of that before lunch, no house playbook is index-flow-keyed (trade-playbooks.md and multi-symbol-sweep.md re-grepped this session for rebalanc|reconstitution|russell|capping|index.flow|IWF|IWY -> zero hits), and an ETF proxy in symbols would make the deterministic screen trip on mega-cap beta. Kind sector matches both the Russell siblings and the S&P entry it pairs with; the enum has no index-flow member and the imperfect fit is named, not fixed from this lane. AMENDED 2026-09-16 BY THIS EVENT'S OWN D-14 PULSE -- A CLASS CORRECTION, NOT A DATE CHANGE. The 2026-09-08 research quoted the Capping Methodology Guide as giving the Russell US Style check an effective date of "Last business day in Mar, Jun, Sep and Dec". Re-fetching the identical artifact (652,008 bytes, 62 streams, sha256 5847553f60a2eaf42350b67341aa34f23458310d2c65abc2f5e17e8429b9d41a, still v5.4 September 2026) and extracting the WHOLE of its section 4.8.6 schedule table rather than one row shows that schedule belongs to the FTSE Emerging ex China RIC 22.5/45 Capped Index and its Net Tax twin. EVERY Russell US Style row -- Russell 1000 Growth/Value, Top 200 Growth/Value, Midcap Growth/Value, 2500, 2000, 3000, 3000E, Top 500, Small Cap Completeness, Microcap -- reads frequency "Monthly", price date "T-3", effective "Last business day of each month", with the trigger unchanged ("No company is greater than 24%, and all companies that have a weight greater than 4.8% in aggregate are no more than 48% of the index", approach Rule 4.2/RIC 22.5/45). THE DATE 2026-09-30 IS UNAFFECTED AND IS NOW DOUBLE-SOURCED rather than single-sourced: 30 September is both the last business day of the month under the guide's standing rule and the July 2026 FAQ's published "Russell US Style Quarter-end Capping Effective Date (open of, if applicable)". Status stays estimate -- the prefix gap is unchanged and this lane may not self-confirm. WHAT THE CORRECTION CHANGES IS THE GENERALISATION, AND IT NARROWS IT: the 4.02% breach probability measured at initial research prices a full quarterly recap landing about 12 sessions ahead of the test, and only four month-ends a year get one. The other eight monthly checks run on a month to a quarter of undisturbed drift and belong nearer the un-reset 28.96% class, so September is among the four cheapest months of the year for this test to fire and 4.02% MUST NOT be inherited by a lane researching an October or November instance. The next check's price date is 2026-10-27, effective 2026-10-30 -- deliberately NOT proposed as a calendar entry, because at 44 days out and low impact it fails assessment-cadence.json's horizon (allImpactsWithinDays 30 admits only critical/high past 30) and a proposal that can never become due is clutter (#2946). Footnote 3's carve-out ("If Russell Reconstitution is scheduled to take effect after the close of the last business day in June ... then the quarter-end capping check will not be performed") is therefore a JUNE-MONTHLY skip, which re-sources the initial research's warning about a 2027-06-30 Russell twin to the correct table row. SECOND MEASUREMENT: AVGO's IWF company weight drifted from 4.96% to about 4.82%, 0.02pp above the 4.8% cohort line and pointing away from a breach; its exit removes about 4.8pp outright. Registered as FT-russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2026-09-30-4. Family AUM re-read from the owner's product screener (as-of 2026-09-15) at $287.4B, from $294.6B -- price, not flows. iShares holdings CSV, stockanalysis.com and Yahoo topHoldings were all blocked to this runner and are recorded in the ledger's probe-ref.blocked rather than substituted silently. AMENDED 2026-09-23 BY THIS EVENT'S OWN D-7 PULSE -- THE FIRST REAL (NON-DRIFTED) POST-RESET HOLDINGS READ CONTRADICTS LEG 5 FOR IWY. Both iShares holdings CSV endpoints that served HTML-only product pages on 09-16 served genuine CSVs this session, dated 2026-09-21 -- the quarterly review's own effective-open date. IWY's over-4.8% company cohort (lines combined per the guide's rule): NVDA 15.13 + AAPL 7.97 + Alphabet(GOOGL 6.04 + GOOG 4.87) 10.91 + MSFT 5.78 + AVGO 5.29 + META 4.93 = 50.01% -- already above the 48% quarter-end trigger itself, four sessions before the 09-25 T-3 price date, and 4.51pp past the 45.5% level FT-russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2026-09-30-2 was registered to test. IWF's cohort: NVDA 15.46 + AAPL 7.74 + Alphabet 10.89 + MSFT 5.43 + AVGO 4.92 = 44.44% -- comfortably under 48%, near its own D-22 estimate (44.62%); the reset assumption failed for IWY without equally failing for IWF. AVGO reads 4.92% (IWF) / 5.29% (IWY) in real data, not the D-14 pulse's drifted ~4.82% that pointed toward an exit -- FT-...-4's kill condition looks headed to fire. META is a newly-crossed sixth cohort member in IWY only (4.93%; 3.89% in IWF, below the line) -- a step-function addition, not a departure. This does not change the event's impact/symbols classification: the fire case stays small in dollar terms and no house playbook applies, but the close-out session (due from 2026-10-01) must treat an IWY breach as the more likely outcome and re-verify every figure here against 09-25-dated holdings before scoring FT-1/FT-2/FT-4, since four sessions of further drift remain.
